analysis.title: The great market puke
key_insights: SPX broke below its 200-day moving average early in the week, took out the longer-term trendline midweek, and is trading below 7,000 (futures). RSI is at its most oversold level since the Liberation Day panic.

MS PB: US L/S hedge fund net exposure fell to 42%, the lowest in a year and the 8th percentile since 2010. Historically, net exposure at this level has coincided with median expected SPX earnings growth of about 5%, with a high of about 10%. Consensus expects 16% earnings growth next year.

GS prime brokerage data: hedge funds are selling Asian AI/tech exposure, with long sales outpacing short sales 2.4 to 1. Korea and Taiwan dominate the selling through both long liquidation and new shorts. Net allocation to Korea is back to early-January levels.

KOSPI volatility has stayed relatively calm despite the sell-off. KOSPI VIX is up from its early October lows but the reaction is muted. The note suggests investors are dumping longs rather than buying puts.

GS (Privorotsky) on SK Hynix: cheap on a blended 24-month P/E, but the risk is earnings sustainability if estimates fall. The valuation cushion makes pressing the short harder, and the note says there may be better places to express a bearish AI and growth view.

GS: Taiwan has seen heavy month-to-date selling from long liquidation and fresh shorts. Net allocation is 4.4% (24th percentile over one year, 85th percentile over five years). Gross allocation is 3.8% (89th percentile over five years).
The Market Ear's EWT December 95 put, flagged less than a month ago as a cheap hedge on a Taiwan catch-down, has gone from about $2 to almost $20, nearly 10x.

DB argues India could be a major beneficiary of AI adoption without winning the race to build it, given nearly 1.5 billion potential users, established digital infrastructure and a large technology workforce.
Gold is at extremely oversold levels. RSI is approaching its lowest readings in decades. The Market Ear says it dislikes catching falling knives but is tempted by the contrarian case.
Gold volatility is rising sharply as price fails to find a bid, with investors buying downside protection.
Silver's weekly RSI has been lower only once since Covid. It fell from above 90 to 30 in almost a straight line.

market_movers.rationale: The December 95 put flagged earlier as a cheap Taiwan downside hedge rose from about $2 to almost $20 as Taiwan equities sold off.

earnings_insights: MS QDS via The Market Ear: consensus expects 16% SPX earnings growth next year. Historically, hedge fund net exposure at the current 42% level has coincided with median expected earnings growth of about 5%, with a high of about 10%.

trade_ideas.description: Long EWT December 95 put (previously highlighted as a cheap Taiwan downside hedge)
trade_ideas.rationale: AI expectations were stretched, positioning was crowded and Korea was under pressure, giving downside convexity.

risk_factors: Earnings sustainability at SK Hynix: cheap valuation can fall further if estimates are cut.
Gap between low hedge fund positioning and 16% consensus earnings growth for next year.
Continued liquidation of Asian AI/tech longs in Korea and Taiwan.
vol_and_positioning: SPX is below its 200-day moving average and below 7,000 (futures), with RSI at its lowest since the Liberation Day panic.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects 16% SPX earnings growth next year, well above the 5% median historically seen at current hedge fund exposure.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge fund net exposure at 42% typically tracks weaker growth expectations, with a historical high of about 10% earnings growth, so consensus may be too high or positioning may be too low.

tension_points.bull_case: The stock looks cheap on a blended 24-month P/E, which makes shorting it harder.
tension_points.bear_case: Cheap can get cheaper if earnings estimates start coming down.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Falling earnings estimates would undermine the valuation-cushion argument.
